Lena (People Ops): Thanks for the great questions during today's all-hands. Putting answers in one place so folks can reference after the meeting. Drop any follow-ups here and I'll loop folks in. :mag:

Jon (Eng): Two quick ones: 1) when do year-end bonuses hit payroll? 2) if I'm promoted mid-cycle, do I get a prorated bonus at the new level?

Lena (People Ops): Good Qs. 1) Year-end bonuses are scheduled to appear on the first regular payroll in January (pay period that includes Jan 15). 2) Promotions approved before the bonus declaration date (Dec 1) will be considered at the new level for bonus calculations; promotions after Dec 1 are prorated based on the time at each level. Finance handles the proration calculations; see Carlos' note below.

Carlos (Finance): Adding: We compute prorated bonus using days-at-level in the calendar year. If you have equity vesting that ties to performance, that remains unchanged unless you have separate equity refreshs approved. Email comp-ops@redwood.com for odd cases.

Sophie (Product): Related: eligibility for equity refresh — is there a minimum tenure after promo before being eligible? Heard different things across teams.

Lena (People Ops): The general guideline: ICs become eligible for refresh discussions 6 months after a promotion. Managers can recommend exceptions during calibration/comp planning windows. Refresh approvals require manager + People Ops + Finance sign-off.

Jon (Eng): Also: mid-search level changes — if we upshift a role from L3->L4 while interviews ongoing, do offers update automatically?

Lena (People Ops): Recruiting should update the req band immediately and add a note to active candidates. If an offer was already accepted but not yet signed, recruiting + manager can reissue an updated offer per the new band (Finance sign-off required). If signed, we do not retroactively change comp unless there's a documented exception.

Sophie (Product): benefits question from a PM: open enrollment window conflicts with new parent's leave. Can they enroll outside window if on leave?

Lena (People Ops): Generally, special enrollment events apply (birth/adoption). If someone goes on parental leave during open enrollment, they are still eligible to enroll during the published window. If they missed it due to a qualifying event, we make adjustments case-by-case. Please DM me and tag @Payroll-Bot so we have the ticket.

Jon (Eng): How do appeals work if an IC thinks their calibration level is wrong? What's the timeline?

Lena (People Ops): Appeals: submit a concise appeal email to people-ops@redwood.com with manager sign-off within 5 business days of the calibration lock date. People Ops + hiring manager + calibration chair review within 7 business days. We're not reopening the full cycle; this is a focused review with potential outcomes: no-change, level update, or manager action plan.

Carlos (Finance): FYI on timing: Any pay adjustments from appeals that are approved after payroll close will hit the next available payroll and may be retroactive per policy. Expect up to 2 pay cycles for manual changes to appear.

Ava (CEO): Quick leadership note: we want to reduce ambiguity around expectations for managers during calibration. Lena, please put together a 2-slide checklist managers must complete before calibration (calibration docs, impact summary, appeals note).

Lena (People Ops): Will do. I'll post the checklist + a short explainer in this channel by Thursday.

Payroll-Bot: Reminder: comp planning materials due to #people-ops by 4/18 17:00 UTC. Upload via the HR portal: https://intranet.redwood.com/hr/comp-planning

Jon (Eng): Thanks everyone. This clears up most of our questions.

Lena (People Ops): Thanks all. If you have a sensitive case, DM me and mention "private appeal". I'll keep this thread pinned for the week. :pushpin:
